programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 35,000 per grant, covering up to 70% of eligible costs; applicant self-financing 30% (de minimis aid).
programmes.deadline_note: Applications can be submitted on a rolling basis; processing takes up to 20 working days.

eligibility.other_note: SME registered in the Estonian Business Register; can apply up to two times; de minimis aid must not exceed EUR 300,000 over three years; project in a RDIE focus area. Application in Estonian only.

programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with the national space agency or regional co-funder
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation with technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support. Some national BICs add local top-up funding.
programmes.deadline_note: This ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. Contact the local centre for the next deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss suitability
Submit application documents before the local deadline
Tender Opening Board review, then presentation to the Tender Evaluation Board
Register a company in Estonia before signing the incubation contract

eligibility.other_note: Business must use space-based systems, apply space technology in a non-space domain, or develop products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in Estonia.

programmes.source_snippet: €50k equity free funding for product and IP development

programmes.amount_note: Maximum EUR 7,500, covering up to 80% of eligible costs; 20% self-financing required.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact EIS customer service with company details and a project overview before applying
Select an eligible service provider (research institution or accredited partner)
Submit the application in the E-toetus portal (in Estonian)
Implement the project and submit the payment claim

eligibility.other_note: Enterprise must be registered in the Estonian Business Register. May apply up to twice. Cannot have received more than EUR 300,000 de minimis aid over the past three years. programmes.source_snippet: Maximum grant EUR 7,500; up to 80% of eligible costs; 20% self-financing by applicant.

programmes.name_en: Grant for cybersecurity innovation and development
programmes.amount_note: EUR 60,000 - 100,000 per grant; page shows self-financing 30%. Aid rate is 70% under de minimis or 45% small / 35% medium / 25% large enterprise under GBER art. 25.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications open 12.01.2026 09:00 to 15.12.2026 16:00 and are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

eligibility.other_note: Estonian-registered company in cybersecurity products/services (EMTAK division K) with a project partner; activities in the EU/EEA. Topics: cybersecurity automation, AI in cybersecurity, post-quantum cryptography migration, space cybersecurity. Co-funded by Digital Europe.

programmes.funder: Prototron (Tallinn Science Park Tehnopol, Swedbank, TalTech)
programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 35,000 equity-free funding for prototype development plus mentoring (winners in recent rounds received EUR 10,000-35,000).
programmes.deadline_note: The application round is currently closed (spring 2026 batch awarded 22 May 2026). Rounds are announced on prototron.ee; an autumn round was launched 30 Sep 2025.

programmes.amount_note: Ecosystem development, mentoring and Startup Visa facilitation rather than direct cash grants to companies.

eligibility.other_note: Residence/visa route, not funding: non-EU founders of a technology-based, innovative, scalable Estonian-registered start-up with an MVP and first traction; company not older than 10 years. State fee EUR 80 (long-stay) or EUR 60 (short-stay).

eligibility.other_note: Strong focus on B2B software from Central and Eastern Europe, the Baltics, the Nordics and Africa. Some in-person residency in Tallinn or another hub is expected.

programmes.deadline_note: Applications on a rolling basis after a mandatory preliminary consultation. Separate defence-sector round of EUR 24M (EUR 250,000-3,000,000) opened 2 March 2026.
